speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To begin your evaluation for acute diarrhea, have you noticed any fever, blood in your stool, or recent travel?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection. Given your history of recent levofloxacin treatment for pneumonia and the development of acute watery diarrhea with cramping, this is highly suggestive of an antibiotic-associated *C. difficile* infection. I will order a stool toxin assay to confirm the diagnosis.
